content.title: EU Antitrust Enforcer Fines Gucci, Chloe, Loewe More Than $180 Million After Pricing Probe
content.summary: The European Union’s competition regulator fined Kering-owned Gucci, LVMH’s Loewe and Richemont’s Chloe fashion labels more than $181.6 million, saying that they engaged in unfair pricing strategies that reduced freedom for distributors.

content.title: Kering Presses Ahead on Sustainability Despite Luxury Downturn
content.summary: As the Institut Français de la Mode celebrated the fifth anniversary of the IFM-Kering Sustainability Chair, the French luxury group's chief sustainability officer Marie-Claire Daveu said new CEO Luca De Meo is uniquely positioned for the challenge.

content.title: European luxury shares rise as creative debuts boost sales hopes
content.summary:
STORY: Shares of European luxury brands rose Tuesday, pushing the industry’s index to its highest level since May.

Designing debuts at fashion houses and fresh pushes for affordability have given investors hope the sector could have a comeback.

The rally was led by French majors.

Kering, Christian Dior and LVMH rose between 3% and 7% in the early afternoon. 

Luxury groups in Europe have tried to turn around a difficult period, where U.S. tariffs and slower demand in China have hit profits.

:: File

New designers at houses of Gucci, Bottega Veneta and Dior presented their collections at last week's Milan Fashion week.

One analyst said investors were “very pleased” with the new collections…

Adding that some luxury brands are reworking price structures to get more affordable products onto shelves. 

Morgan Stanley analysts have also bet on what it calls a "burst of creativity” in the industry. 

They upgraded recommendations for Kering and LVMH in a note to investors.

content.title: Morgan Stanley upgrades LVMH stock, Kering becomes new top pick in luxury
content.summary: Investing.com -- Morgan Stanley has upgraded shares of LVMH and Kering to Overweight, making Kering its new top pick in the luxury sector, while downgrading Hermès and Prada to Equal-weight, citing a “creative supply shock” reshaping the industry.

content.title: Gucci Names Second CEO in Less Than a Year as It Struggles to Revive Sales
content.summary: Kering appointed Francesca Bellettini as Gucci’s latest chief executive, reshuffling its leadership for the second time in less than a year as the flagship brand struggles to revive sales.

content.title: Kering's new boss de Meo appoints Bellettini to lead Gucci revival
content.summary: French luxury group Kering has named Francesca Bellettini as chief executive of Gucci, replacing Stefano Cantino after only nine months at the Italian fashion brand.  Placing Bellettini directly in charge of Gucci, which she previously oversaw from Paris as deputy Kering CEO, marks Chief Executive Luca de Meo's first major move since taking the helm last week.  Bellettini had been deputy CEO in charge of brand development since 2023 alongside Jean-Marc Duplaix, who Kering said would stay on as chief operating officer.
